questions.stem: A woman introduces a man by saying, 'He is the son of the woman who is the mother of my husband.' How is the man related to the woman?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Mother of my husband = my mother-in-law. Son of my mother-in-law = my husband's brother = my brother-in-law. Trap: 'Son' would require the man to be her own child, not her husband's sibling; 'Uncle' would require a generational gap not present here.

questions.stem: Pointing to a photograph, a man says, 'She is the daughter of my grandfather's only son.' How is the woman in the photograph related to the man?
questions.explanation: C is correct. My grandfather's only son = my father (assuming the man himself is from this lineage). Daughter of my father = my sister. Trap: 'Cousin' would apply if grandfather had multiple sons; 'Niece' would require the man to be one generation above; 'Daughter' would require the woman to be his child.

questions.stem: P is the father of Q. Q is the brother of R. R is the mother of S. What is P's relationship to S?
questions.explanation: C is correct. P → Q (father). Q and R are siblings (Q = brother of R). Therefore P is also R's father. R → S (mother). So P is the father of R (who is S's mother) → P is S's maternal grandfather. Trap: 'Uncle' confuses the step where P is deduced to be R's father; 'Father' skips a generation.

questions.stem: Introducing a woman to a guest, a man says, 'She is the wife of the only son of my mother.' How is the woman related to the man?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Only son of my mother = me (the man himself, assuming he is the only son). Wife of me = my wife. Trap: 'Sister-in-law' would apply if his mother had more than one son; 'Sister' is incorrect since the woman is a wife, not a sibling.

questions.stem: A says to B, 'Your father's sister is my mother.' How is A related to B?
questions.explanation: B is correct. B's father's sister = B's aunt. A's mother is B's father's sister. So A's mother is B's aunt → A is B's aunt's child = B's cousin. Trap: 'Brother' would require A and B to share the same parents; 'Nephew' reverses the generational relationship.

questions.stem: In a code: A × B means 'A is the mother of B'; A + B means 'A is the father of B'; A − B means 'A is the brother of B'. In the expression P × Q + R, what is P's relationship to R?
questions.explanation: B is correct. P × Q: P is the mother of Q. Q + R: Q is the father of R. So P is Q's mother and Q is R's father. Therefore P is R's paternal grandmother. Trap: 'Mother' skips a generation; 'Aunt' would require P to be a sibling of R's parent, not a parent herself.

questions.stem: M is the son of N. N is the daughter of O. O is the father of P. How is P related to M?
questions.explanation: C is correct. N is O's daughter and M is N's son. O is also P's father (O is the father of P). So N and P are both O's children → N and P are siblings. Since N is M's mother, P is M's maternal uncle (if P is male) or maternal aunt (if P is female). The relationship is Uncle or Aunt. Trap: 'Grandfather' would require O to be M's grandfather, but O is P's father (one generation above P, and P is M's uncle/aunt — so O is M's grandfather ✓). Wait — rechecking: O is N's father (so O is M's maternal grandfather ✓) and O is P's father (so P is N's sibling = M's uncle/aunt ✓). Answer: C (Uncle or Aunt) is correct for P's relationship to M.

questions.stem: Pointing to a man in a photograph, a woman says, 'His mother is the only daughter of my mother.' How is the man related to the woman?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Only daughter of my mother = myself (the woman is the only daughter of her mother). So the man's mother is the woman herself. The man is the woman's son. Trap: 'Nephew' would apply if the woman's only daughter is her sister's daughter; 'Brother' misidentifies the gender/generation relationship.

questions.stem: In a code: A ÷ B means 'A is the father of B'; A − B means 'A is the wife of B'; A × B means 'A is the brother of B'. In the expression P ÷ R − Q, how is Q related to P?
questions.explanation: C is correct. P ÷ R: P is the father of R. R − Q: R is the wife of Q. So P is R's father, and R is Q's wife. Therefore P is Q's father-in-law, and Q is P's son-in-law. Trap: 'Daughter-in-law' confuses who married whom — Q is male (R is Q's wife), so Q is P's son-in-law, not daughter-in-law.

questions.stem: X has two children — Y (son) and Z (daughter). Y is married to W and has a son V. Z is married to U and has a daughter T. How is T related to V?
questions.explanation: C is correct. V is Y's son → V is X's grandson. T is Z's daughter → T is X's granddaughter. Y and Z are siblings (both children of X). Since V's father (Y) and T's mother (Z) are siblings, V and T are cousins. Trap: 'Sister' would require same parents; 'Niece' would require V to be one generation above T's parent (he is not — V and T are the same generation).
